It's been quite a while since last summer's misadventures in container gardening - here's an update:

  • We moved! With a new location come new conditions and new challenges.

Our new place is under Zone 5A in the central US. It's a lowland area, with lots of water and scads of outhouse lilies growing all over. Wild grapevines are strangling the trees and roadsides, and there are signs of drainage issues: standing water in a bordering field, and whole sections of sidewalk that have sunk beneath the grassline. Because it's an apartment we're somewhat limited in our ability to make changes, but a large open patio has given us great space for container planting.

The fenceline of our place has about 200 yards of fruiting blackberries, and a mulberry tree has been dropping fruit all month! Pretty soon we'll have filled our second gallon of berry harvest - and I need to figure out how to get those blackberries in a more organized state.

  • A week of downpour has left us in pretty rough shape.

June started with a half-flat of tomatoes, peppers, alyssum and petunias to get me started. After languishing in a greenhouse until June they were rootbound, so I transplanted these into fiber pots - I didn't have the budget for much else. From the farm I also brought a nice healthy tomatillo, an eggplant and some basil.

We had nearly a week of solid rain, which took a heavy toll on all the greenhouse plants. My peppers and alyssum seem to have shaken it off, but the petunias got knocked out hard. The tomatoes were all planted up to their necks together in a large pot - tomatoes are good at converting roots to stems and vice versa, so hopefully they'll recover.

  • We got a late start on things, but we're still trying.

We moved in mid-May so I didn't really prepare anything like I should have. It's June, and I'm buying seeds! What the heck, let's go for it. I bought some amaranth, creeping thyme, and lupine as things to fill out all my fiber pots. My lovely assistant did a wonderful job helping me set the seeds. In the next couple weeks we'll see how well they germinated.

  • We have a mystery plant! Help me identify it, so we can keep it alive!

Some relatives from down in Nevada sent us a succulent that's absolutely gorgeous, however we can't figure out what the heck it even IS, much less what to do with it. It's planted in very light high-drainage stuff, so we're just going to give it a ton of sun and avoid getting it too wet. It's pretty though!
